characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Bruker D8 Advance X-ray diffractometer, Cu target, continuous scanning, 30–100°, 2°/min
characterization_methods.key_findings: P-150 pattern contains only γ-Fe(M) fcc reflections (111, 200, 220, 311, 222) with no α-Fe(M); the full width at half maximum (FWHM) of the (111) peak for P-150 is 0.237.
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine phase constitution of the SLM-printed P-150 alloy

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Oxford Symmetry S2 EBSD, step size 0.3–0.7 μm, accelerating voltage 15–20 kV; analyzed with TSL OIM software
characterization_methods.key_findings: P-150 transverse cross-section shows coarse equiaxed grains with randomly mixed orientations and no dominant texture (Fig. 7(e)).
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize grain morphology and orientation in the P-150 cross-section
characterization_methods.technique: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) inverse pole figures

characterization_methods.key_findings: P-150 shows Porosity=0.35% with numerous dark defects, several elongated/needle-like, one labelled 'Crack'.

P-150 (150 W) surface shows multiple spherical droplets and the label 'Balling' (localized heat accumulation); the P-150 fracture surface (Fig. 13(e)) shows cracks labelled 'Crack' together with dimple and cleavage features, evidencing internal defects and spheroidization.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: surface morphology and tensile fracture surfaces, 200 μm / 20 μm scale bars
characterization_methods.purpose: Study surface quality and tensile fracture morphology

characterization_methods.key_findings: P-150 average hardness 281 HV (cross-section) and 283 HV (longitudinal section).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load 0.5 kg for 10 s; arithmetic mean of five points; cross-section and longitudinal section
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure average hardness of cross and longitudinal sections

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Suns universal testing machine with Reliant electronic extensometer
characterization_methods.key_findings: P-150: yield strength 771.5 MPa, tensile strength 1032.0 MPa, elongation 28.28%.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; loading rate 1 mm/min; dog-bone specimen, gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm

characterization_methods.key_findings: P-150 surface roughness Sa = 4.19 μm (Fig. 10(e)); surface becomes smoother with increasing laser power.
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure surface roughness Sa of P-150

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Compared to the as-cast sample, the SLM-printed P-150 sample has higher tensile strength (1032.0 vs 879.0 MPa) and comparable yield strength (771.5 vs 772.3 MPa), which is attributed to grain-refining strengthening from rapid cooling during SLM.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The substrate was heated to 200 °C prior to printing.

processing_steps.atmosphere: argon (99.99% pure), oxygen content in forming chamber maintained below 300 ppm
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Printed on an SLM Solutions SLM280 printer (samples 75×12×12 mm and 10×10×10 mm). Laser power 150 W corresponding to laser energy density 125.00 J/mm³ (the parameter defining sample P-150); spot diameter 0.1 mm; layer thickness 0.02 mm; hatch space 0.08 mm; scanning speed 750 mm/s; overlapping-strip scanning strategy with a 67° rotation angle applied to each layer.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Suns universal testing machine; Reliant electronic extensometer
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: dog-bone-shaped tensile sample with a gauge length of 25 mm and a diameter of 5 mm

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Fig. 12 (engineering stress–strain curve for P-150, purple); shows a steep elastic rise followed by a long nearly flat plastic plateau above 1000 MPa and an abrupt vertical fracture drop.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Microhardness tester at a load of 0.5 kg for 10 s; each value is the arithmetic mean of five measurement points

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Right-skewed distribution; lowest modal bar of the cross-sectional series (just above the 8% fraction gridline); flatter and more extended than the lower-power samples, with a secondary cluster of grains near 16–24 μm and the fraction of large grains growing with laser power (Fig. 8(e)).
grain_structure.texture: random orientations, no preferred texture (equiaxed grains)

phases_present.texture: random orientations, no dominant/strong crystallographic texture

precipitates.distribution: uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix (as established for SLM-printed samples)

structures.overall_structure: SLM-printed Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni (P-150) consists mainly of austenite (γ-Fe(M), fcc) with no α-Fe(M) ferrite, plus a small amount of nano-sized κ carbide. The transverse cross-section reveals fine-to-coarse equiaxed grains with random orientations and no strong crystallographic texture (fine equiaxed grains attributed to the 67° interlayer rotation).

unmapped_findings: P-150 surface roughness Sa = 4.19 μm (b0044, figure_010(e)).

The minimum density among all samples prepared with different parameters is 6.78 g/cm³, much lighter than 304 stainless steel (7.93 g/cm³); this value is reported for the sample set as a whole and is not attributed specifically to P-150 (b0023).

FWHM of the (111) γ-Fe(M) diffraction peak for P-150 = 0.237; FWHM decreases with increasing laser power, implying the average grain size of SLM-printed samples gradually increases with energy density (b0033).
The substrate for printing was heated to 200 °C and argon (99.99% pure) was used with oxygen maintained below 300 ppm (b0020).
